name: Manage shop drawings and submittals
summary: Before trades fabricate or order materials, they send shop drawings, product data and samples to the general contractor, which checks them against the drawings and specifications, stamps them and sends them to the design consultant for review. The assistant project manager logs, chases and distributes, the field engineer reviews and coordinates, and the consultant and its engineers return a status. Long consultant reviews, incomplete packages and resubmission loops delay procurement of long-lead items and can push the schedule.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor of about 2,800 employees building institutional, commercial and industrial buildings, with about 220 active projects run from regional offices, a web-based project management platform and a construction ERP.
baseline.notes: Practice described for Ontario stipulated-price and construction-management projects on CCDC contract forms; Western and Atlantic projects follow the same pattern under their provincial lien and safety laws.

unit_of_work: one submittal (one shop drawing, product data or sample package for a specification section)
trigger: A subcontractor or supplier sends a submittal package for review.
end_state: The reviewed submittal is released to the trade for fabrication or ordering, placed in the field set and filed for closeout.

volume.seasonality: Submittals peak in the first third of each project after subcontract award, so company volume follows project starts; slightly higher in late winter and spring when summer-season projects are bought out.

evidence.note: Kept from the organisation file: about 13 submittals per active project per month, consistent with 250 to 400 submittals over a 22-month institutional project. Counting resubmissions as separate cases would raise it by about 30%; here resubmissions loop within one case.
Share of the role's time on submittals, author's estimate; headcount from the organisation file. 120 field engineers x about 0.27.
Share of the role's time on submittals, author's estimate; headcount from the organisation file. 140 assistant project managers x 0.2.
Share of the role's time on submittals, author's estimate; headcount from the organisation file. 110 project managers x about 0.02.

Share of the role's time on submittals, author's estimate; headcount from the organisation file. 120 superintendents x about 0.025; superintendents run mock-up reviews though the organisation file does not list them on this process.

systems.name: Project management platform (drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, change events)
BIM and clash detection tools (Revit, Navisworks)
CPM scheduling software (Primavera P6, Microsoft Project)

resources.name: Telehandlers, skid steers and aerial work platforms

steps.name: Log the incoming submittal
steps.description: The assistant project manager receives the shop drawings, product data or sample transmittal from the trade or supplier, gives it a number against the specification section, attaches the files in the project platform and sets the internal and consultant due dates from the submittal schedule.

error.defect_description: Submittal is logged against the wrong specification section.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; 2019-2022 submittals arrived as PDFs by email or through the platform.

steps.name: Check the package is complete
steps.description: The assistant project manager checks that every item in the specification section is included, that the trade has stamped and signed its own review, that drawings are legible and to scale, and that samples or colour charts are attached where required.

error.defect_description: Missing items are not noticed until the consultant review.

evidence.note: About one package in ten returned before technical review; author's estimate.

steps.name: Trade completes or revises the package
steps.description: The subcontractor or supplier's detailer adds the missing items or revises the drawings to the comments, re-stamps them and sends a new revision; the GC waits and chases if the revision is late.

evidence.note: Detailers take a few days to three weeks to revise, longer for structural steel and precast; author's estimate. Detailer hours are outside the organisation and not counted.

steps.name: Review against drawings and specifications
steps.description: The field engineer compares the submittal with the contract drawings, specifications, coordinated model and reviewed submittals of adjoining trades, checks dimensions, products, performance data and connections, and marks up deviations and questions.

error.defect_description: A deviation from the specification or a clash with another trade is missed.

next.condition: affects other trades or the model
major problems, returned to the trade

evidence.note: CCDC 2 makes the contractor responsible for errors in shop drawings (GC 3.10.10, src pawson); Chin found long reviews come from insufficient and unclear information (src iglc). Times and branch shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Coordinate the submittal with other trades
steps.description: For mechanical, electrical, structural steel, precast and similar packages the field engineer overlays the drawings on the coordinated model or adjoining trades' reviewed submittals and resolves clashes with the trades before submission.

error.defect_description: A clash is resolved on paper but not with the trade.

evidence.note: About 30% of submittals need multi-trade coordination; author's estimate.

steps.name: Apply the contractor's review stamp
steps.description: The assistant project manager confirms the field engineer's review is complete, applies the general contractor's review stamp with the reviewer's name and date to the PDF, and attaches the GC markups for the consultant.

error.defect_description: Submittal is stamped without the field engineer's review.

control.basis: CCDC 2 GC 3.10: contractor reviews shop drawings before submission and remains responsible for errors and omissions (GC 3.10.10)

evidence.note: Contract duty from CCDC 2 GC 3.10 as summarised in src pawson; time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Transmit to the consultant
steps.description: The project platform sends the stamped submittal to the consultant's contract administrator with a transmittal, records the date and starts the review clock; where the consultant uses its own portal the assistant project manager uploads it there as well.

evidence.note: Some project offices batch transmittals once a day; author's estimate.

steps.name: Consultant and sub-consultants review
steps.description: The architect reviews for general conformance with the design intent and routes structural, mechanical and electrical packages to the responsible engineer, who marks up the drawings and returns them with a review status.

error.defect_description: A comment adds scope without being identified as a change.

control.basis: Architect or professional engineer reviews shop drawings for conformance with design intent (CCDC 2 GC 3.10.12)

evidence.note: Contracts allow 10 working days to 21 days (EJCDC not less than 14 days, a 21-day clause, src csi; CCDC 2 'reasonable promptness', src pawson); design teams observed averaging 28 to 42 or more days on some projects (src csi). Mode 9 days, mean about 13 days.

steps.name: Chase the overdue submittal
steps.description: The assistant project manager emails the consultant with the list of overdue submittals and the dates materials are needed, raises them at the weekly consultant meeting, and warns that late reviews will delay fabrication.

evidence.note: Weekly meeting cadence; author's estimate.

steps.name: Consultant returns the review after the chase
steps.description: After the reminder the consultant finishes the review, often after a sub-consultant has returned its markups, and sends the submittal back with its review status.

evidence.note: Late reviews of four to six weeks reported in src csi; range is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Log the returned submittal and its status
steps.description: The assistant project manager records the return date and status (reviewed, reviewed as noted, revise and resubmit, or rejected) in the submittal log and decides whether it goes back to the trade for revision or forward for release.

error.defect_description: Status keyed wrongly; a rejected item is released.

evidence.note: About a quarter of first submissions need resubmission on building projects; author's estimate (no source with a measured rate was found).

steps.name: Return the submittal to the trade for resubmission
steps.description: The assistant project manager sends the consultant's markups to the trade with a request to revise and resubmit by a set date, and flags the item on the lookahead if fabrication or installation depends on it.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Check consultant comments for scope and cost
steps.description: The field engineer reads every consultant comment, checks whether any comment changes the work beyond the contract documents or affects another trade, and flags those to the project manager.

error.defect_description: A scope-adding comment is not flagged.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the share of reviews whose comments change scope.

steps.name: Decide on a change from review comments
steps.description: The project manager compares the comment with the contract documents and decides whether to give notice of a change to the consultant before the trade proceeds, or to accept the comment as clarification within the contract.

control.basis: CCDC 2 GC 3.10.9: deviations accepted in writing; Part 6 change notice before proceeding

evidence.note: CCDC 2 GC 3.10.9 as summarised in src pawson; time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Distribute the reviewed submittal and release fabrication
steps.description: The assistant project manager sends the reviewed submittal to the trade with written release to fabricate or order, copies the superintendent and supply chain, and notes any long-lead item whose delivery date needs tracking.

error.defect_description: Trade fabricates to an earlier revision.

next.condition: sample or mock-up required on site

evidence.note: Long-lead and mock-up shares are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Track fabrication and delivery of a long-lead item
steps.description: The assistant project manager asks the trade or supplier for a fabrication slot and delivery date, enters it in the procurement log and the schedule, and checks it against the date the superintendent needs the material on site.

error.defect_description: Delivery date slips without the schedule being updated.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Build and inspect a sample or mock-up on site
steps.description: The superintendent arranges for the trade to install a sample panel, masonry or envelope mock-up, books the consultant's site visit, walks the mock-up with the architect and records acceptance or required changes.

error.defect_description: Mock-up accepted verbally without a record.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; consultant visits are weekly or fortnightly.

steps.name: Put the reviewed copy in the field set
steps.description: The field engineer adds the reviewed shop drawing to the current field set in the platform and the trailer, removes superseded revisions, and tells the superintendent which areas can now be built.

error.defect_description: A superseded revision stays in the field set.

evidence.note: Poor project information causes 22% of rework (src cdive); time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Close the submittal and file it for closeout
steps.description: The project platform marks the submittal closed with its final status and date, and tags product data and shop drawings that must go into the operations and maintenance manuals at closeout.

evidence.note: Automatic in the platform.

exceptions.name: Revise and resubmit
exceptions.description: The consultant returns the submittal as revise and resubmit or rejected, and the trade revises it; the loop repeats the GC review and the consultant review.

exceptions.name: Incomplete package returned before review
exceptions.description: The assistant project manager returns a package missing items or the trade's own stamp.

exceptions.name: Overdue consultant review
exceptions.description: The consultant misses the review period and the assistant project manager chases weekly.

exceptions.name: Mock-up required
exceptions.description: Envelope, masonry and finish items need an on-site mock-up accepted by the architect before production.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from first receipt from the trade to release

evidence.note: Built from contract review periods of 10 working days to 21 days (src csi, src pawson) plus several days of GC review, with about a quarter of items resubmitted once; the p90 reflects consultants averaging 28 to 42 days on some projects (src csi).

pain_points.description: Consultant reviews run past the contract period, delaying fabrication slots for long-lead items such as steel, precast, switchgear and air handlers.

evidence.note: Averages of 28 to 42 or more days observed (src csi); steel and rebar reviews unnecessarily long (src iglc).

pain_points.description: Incomplete or unclear packages from trades cause rejections and resubmission loops.

evidence.note: Root cause of long reviews is insufficient and unclear information.

pain_points.description: GC review is rushed by field engineers who also do layout and RFIs, so errors reach the consultant or the field.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from practice.

pain_points.description: Superseded revisions stay in the field set and crews build to the wrong drawing.

evidence.note: Poor project information causes 22% of rework.

sources.title: Stipulated Price Contract
sources.publisher: Canadian Consulting Engineer (Owen Pawson, Miller Thomson)
sources.supports: CCDC 2-2008: consultant reviews shop drawings with reasonable promptness so as to cause no delay (GC 3.10.12) and indicates acceptance or rejection of deviations in writing (GC 3.10.9); the contractor remains responsible for errors or omissions in shop drawings (GC 3.10.10); the consultant has 20 calendar days after the contractor submits an application and a list of items to be completed or corrected to verify substantial performance (GC 5.4.2); payment certificates within 10 calendar days (GC 5.3.1).

sources.title: Shop drawings and submittals: timeliness of submittal reviews
sources.supports: Design teams observed averaging 28 days and 42 or more days to respond to submittals; example contract clause giving the architect 21 days; EJCDC language allowing not less than 14 days for engineer's review with more for large or complex submittals; simple submittals may need two or three days.

sources.title: Identifying Root Causes of Long Review Times for Engineering Shop Drawings
sources.publisher: International Group for Lean Construction, IGLC-17 (Chang-Sun Chin)
sources.supports: Review times for structural steel and reinforcing bar shop drawings are unnecessarily long and often miss contractors' expected response times; the root cause is insufficient and unclear information rather than reviewer capability or availability.

sources.title: Industry could be overspending $177B per year, study finds
sources.supports: FMI and PlanGrid 'Construction Disconnected' survey of 600 professionals (49% general contractors): 35% of time on non-optimal activities, more than 14 hours per person per week; 5.5 hours a week looking for project data, almost 5 hours managing disagreements, nearly 4 hours on mistakes needing rework; poor communication 26% and poor project information 22% of rework.

assumptions: The simulated median of about 25 days is above the 21-day benchmark mainly because of the resubmission loop (about a quarter of cases) and day-long internal queues; both are tier C estimates and the gap is within the range the sources allow (consultant averages of 28 to 42 days on slow projects).
One case is one submittal package; resubmissions are loops within the case, not new cases.
Consultant, sub-consultant and trade detailer time is outside the organisation and given zero touch time, so the staffing check covers company staff only.
No source opened gives a measured resubmission rate; 25% is the author's estimate for building projects.
Rebar shop drawings and concrete mix designs for self-performed work come from suppliers (12% of triggers); the organisation file lists only subcontractors as the trigger.
Review comments that change scope (about 7% of cases) produce a change request to ops-change-order; the organisation file has no such link.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (1.35 loading factor for salaried staff).
US contract periods (EJCDC, AIA-style clauses) from src csi are used beside CCDC 2 because CCDC 2-2008 sets no fixed period and CCDC 2-2020 moved timing to Division 01.
